meta.description: Batch effect correction for CRISPR screens covering ComBat empirical-Bayes, RUV, SVA, control-sgRNA normalization, and the model-based alternative of including batch as a covariate in MAGeCK MLE or Chronos, plus diagnosis, decision-tree guidance, and when correction harms biology.

scientific_integrity.detail: All cited references (Johnson 2007 Biostatistics, Leek 2012 Bioinformatics, Risso 2014 Nat Biotechnol, Pacini 2021 Nat Commun, Vinceti 2024 Genome Biol) are real, correctly attributed landmark papers. No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or results in any of the 7 outputs; all quantitative results (AUCs, betas, correlations) trace to real HAP1 TKOv3 data or clearly-labeled synthetic data with disclosed ground truth.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure computational-biology screen analysis; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or clinical claims about individuals anywhere in scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Confounding, covariate modeling, and empirical-Bayes assumptions are handled correctly throughout (Input 3 correctly distinguishes 'destroys biology' from 'tool refuses' rather than conflating them).

code_usability.detail: Every input's FINAL delivered code ran to completion with no syntax errors, infinite loops, or missing dependencies. Caveat carried in P1 recommendations, not this gate: SKILL.md's own combat_correct() and RUV cIdx snippets crash exactly as literally written (Inputs 1 and 2) until a 1-line type fix is applied, and ComBat silently returns all-NaN output (not an exception) when forced on batch-free data (Input 7). None of these are syntax errors, infinite loops, or missing dependencies -- the strict M4 bar -- so this gate does not fire, but the underlying defects are real and scored down in static and dynamic scoring.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness are strong (full coverage of ComBat/RUV/SVA/NTC/covariate methods, well-matched to the domain), but Correctness is docked hard: 2 of the 5 documented code patterns (ComBat's 'Critical' mod usage, RUV's cIdx) crash as literally written.

reliability.note: Version-Compatibility section anticipates API drift and tells the agent to adapt, which is good design intent, but there is zero guidance for the far more dangerous silent-NaN failure mode found in Input 7, and error reporting for the two code bugs is raw library tracebacks with no Skill-level pointer to the fix.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is dense but relevant (282 lines, no padding); usage-guide.md carries the deeper examples. Workflow is linear with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Consistent terminology, an explicit Validation Checklist, and 'Critical' callouts before common mistakes are strong; docked slightly because the ComBat covariate call requires debugging despite being flagged as the single most important pattern to get right.

human_usability.note: Description is trigger-rich and natural; Forgiveness is limited because failures surface as raw stack traces (Python TypeError / R S4 dispatch error) rather than Skill-level guidance, and per Category-3 scene override this is scored on error clarity, not on strictness.

security.note: No credential or data-safety issues. Docked on Input Validation: none of the documented functions validate the type/shape of batch_vector, condition_vector, or mod before use, which is the direct root cause of two of the three bugs found.

maintainability.note: Functions are small and single-purpose with clear parameters (good Modularity/Modifiability); Testability is docked because the inline SKILL.md snippets show no sign of having been run against the real installed pyComBat/RUVSeq APIs before shipping (examples/batch_correct.py, which does run, sidesteps ComBat and RUV entirely).

agent_specific.note: Excellent Composability (7 accurately-described Related Skills links) and Progressive Disclosure; strong Escape Hatches (When NOT to Correct table) docked one point because that table doesn't warn the escape hatch can be bypassed into a silent 100%-NaN outcome if a user overrides it.

key_strengths: SVA and MAGeCK-MLE-covariate patterns ran perfectly out-of-the-box against real HAP1 TKOv3 data, recovering known essential genes (POLR2L, POLR3H, PCNA, MRPL53, RRM1) even under a planted batch shift, concordant with this environment's independent MAGeCK/BAGEL2/drugZ smoke tests on the same dataset.

The confounded-batch failure mode the Skill warns about is real and precisely reproducible: forcing ComBat without a covariate on batch-confounded data collapsed essential-gene signal (AUC 0.945 -> 0.831), and pycombat's own confound detector correctly refuses when a covariate is added instead.
Decision-tree framing (When NOT to Correct, Common Errors, Quantitative Thresholds) gives an agent clear, checkable stop conditions rather than blanket 'always correct' guidance.
Composability is strong: accurate, specific 'Related Skills' links to mageck-analysis, screen-qc, copy-number-correction, library-design, jacks-analysis, hit-calling, and in-vivo-screens.

recommendations.title: ComBat combat_correct() crashes on its own 'Critical' covariate usage
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's combat_correct() passes mod as a one-hot numpy array and data as a raw array; pycombat requires mod as a plain list and data as a DataFrame, so the documented function raises an error on the exact call pattern the Skill labels 'Critical'.
recommendations.root_cause: The example was written against pyComBat's docstring assumption rather than executed against the installed API; pycombat's mod contract (a list, one-hot-encoded internally) is easy to misread as 'pass a pre-encoded matrix'.
recommendations.fix: Change combat_correct() to pass data=pd.DataFrame(log_data, index=..., columns=...) and mod=list(condition_vector); add a smoke test asserting the returned DataFrame has zero NaNs.

recommendations.title: RUV example's cIdx type is incompatible with SeqExpressionSet dispatch
recommendations.problem: ntc_indices <- which(rownames(counts_df) %in% ntc_sgrna_names) returns integer positions, but RUVg's S4 method for x='SeqExpressionSet' only accepts cIdx='character' (control rownames); the documented snippet fails with an S4 dispatch error on first use.
recommendations.root_cause: The which()-based indexing pattern matches RUVg's x='matrix' method (cIdx='ANY') but not the stricter x='SeqExpressionSet' method shown two lines earlier in the same snippet.
recommendations.fix: Use ntc_indices <- rownames(counts_df)[rownames(counts_df) %in% ntc_sgrna_names] (character rownames) before calling RUVg on a SeqExpressionSet.

recommendations.title: Forcing ComBat on a batch-free design silently returns 100% NaN
recommendations.problem: When replicate correlation is already >0.95 within and across batches and a user overrides the Skill's 'no correction needed' guidance, pycombat's empirical-Bayes variance step divides by a near-zero pooled variance and returns an all-NaN DataFrame with exit code 0 and no exception.
recommendations.root_cause: Neither combat_correct() nor the Validation Checklist includes a basic NaN/Inf sanity check on ComBat's output; only downstream biological checks (PCA overlap, PR-AUC) are specified, which a user would only run after already trusting a corrupted matrix.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit post-hoc check to combat_correct() (assert not corrected.isna().any().any()) and a Common Errors row: 'ComBat output is all-NaN -> batch effect too small to estimate a pooled variance; do not force correction, see When NOT to Correct.'

recommendations.title: No explicit out-of-CRISPR-screen scope boundary
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md never states whether its ComBat/RUV/SVA guidance is intended to generalize to non-CRISPR batch correction (e.g. bulk RNA-seq); an agent must infer this solely from the frontmatter description.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill documents only positive guidance for screens, with no negative/boundary section for adjacent domains.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Related but out of scope' note: the underlying statistical methods generalize, but the quantitative thresholds (NTC count, CEGv2 PR-AUC) and MAGeCK/Chronos integration are CRISPR-screen-specific.

recommendations.title: MAGeCK MLE permutation p-values are not flagged as run-to-run stochastic
recommendations.problem: mageck mle's default permutation-based significance testing is not seeded by the documented command, so p-values/FDR can vary slightly between reruns on identical input; the batch-covariate example doesn't mention this.
recommendations.root_cause: The example focuses on design-matrix mechanics and omits mageck mle's own reproducibility caveats.
recommendations.fix: Note that beta estimates are stable but permutation p-values are stochastic unless a seed/round count is fixed, and reference mageck mle's own --permutation-round option.
